utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries, therefore the witness can be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dodik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Tieger will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dodik, and everyone in the courtroom. Mr. Dodik, just before we adjourned yesterday, you had been shown a portion of a transcript from a December 1991 session of the SFRY Presidency in connection with my question to you about the lists of steps or moves that Mr. Karadzic had and waited for opportune moments to implement. You indicated that you did not attend that Presidency session. I wanted then to move to 65 ter 02390, page 74 in the English and page 57 of the Serbian. And that, Mr. Dodik, is the 38th Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly. And at the bottom of the page in both languages, Mr. Karadzic says the following: "Let us use Alija's mistake to increase the price of wine, remember how all the SAOs," that is the Serbian Autonomous Regions, "and all those measures before the war always took place following Alija's mistakes; there were 9-10 actions that we carried out," we turn to the next page in English. I know we're about to turn to the next page in Serbian, "that we carried them out. We brain-stormed them all together, however, we did not pull all nine moves straight away but we carried them out after Alija made a mistake, it is then that we would make a move and the Muslims would curse his mother afterwards and not ours." So do you remember these remarks of Mr. Karadzic at the 38th Assembly, Mr. Dodik?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Do you know whether you were at that session or not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only see here that it's Mr. Karadzic speaking. I don't know what session it was and where it was held, but that's included in the minutes. But I don't remember. I really don't know and I cannot say only on the basis of this whether I was present or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I don't remember. I don't remember any of this. And to me it seems just like empty praise and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik, would you refrain from commenting on it. You don't remember. You've answered the question. There's no need to comment as you did. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 02390 receives number P7762.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The moves and steps that Dr. Karadzic was referring to at the 38th Session and also at the SFRY Presidency included most of the major steps on the path toward the establishment of the republic, that is, the association of communities, Serbian Autonomous Region, establishment of the Assembly, and so on. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was such a time that certainly we did make certain moves, and they were completely legitimate from the view of establishing Republika Srpska. Since Yugoslavia broke up using the people's right to self-determination, which was set out in the constitution of SFRY, the Serbs were entitled to have their own territorial organisation. That was how it was understood and how I understood it. So moves of this character constituting an entity were fully legitimate, but they were always a reaction to something else. That's also true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, that's how we began the discussion, Mr. Dodik, and I put to you that what you're calling a reaction and what Dr. Karadzic liked to refer to as a reaction was, in fact, the implementation of pre-planned steps. And again in that connection, let's turn to P6999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that, Mr. Tieger --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- with P7762, I'd forgotten to ask you how many pages there were and there were 96, I see now. Could you reduce that to the portion that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course. Yeah. And in circumstances like that, I -- it's -- it's taken as a given that we will reduce it to the appropriate portion, but I'm sorry I didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But of course the Chamber should know --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what will be admitted into evidence, and at this moment you have 96 pages so that will be reduced. We hear from you in the next two days or perhaps even today. Meanwhile, we have the document you called up on our screens. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik, this is an interview given by Dr. Karadzic on the 6th of January, 1995, to Srpska Oslobodjenje. And at page 3 in the English and page 2 in Serbian, at the upper portion of the column at the far left, Dr. Karadzic stated the following: "We had a list of the actions and steps to take but we always waited for the Muslims to make a mistake; and after they made one, we created a union of municipalities and the Serbian autonomous areas next, followed by the regions and eventually our assembly and, finally, republic." Mr. Dodik, that's another reflection of Dr. Karadzic's repeated insistence and emphasis on the fact that he had all the steps prepared in advance and he waited for opportune moments to implement them; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have such an impression. I think that this is just a PR explanation given by Karadzic at the time. I had no impression that there was an organised plan, especially in terms of municipalities. I think that municipalities were established by the people on the ground rather than that it was anything pre-planned. It was only later that policies that were a response to current events were promoted, and I think that this was fully legitimate. In any case, both the community of municipalities and forming of the republic later on in view of the situation that the Serbian people were in, I think that this would have been done even if Mr. Karadzic had not been the president. That was --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the question is not whether you consider it to have been justified or legitimate or not, just whether or not that was the case, and I think you've addressed your position on that. Now, you said you considered this to be some kind of public relations gesture in 1995, but this Court has received evidence that, for example, in January of 1992 Dr. Karadzic, in a telephone conversation with Nenad Stevandic, said: "We have all the moves in the envelopes..." and then said "we have plans for everything. They," referring to some of the local Krajina leaders, "just keep running ahead like oxen after salt." That's D857, pages 6 through 7, but let me show you a similar discussion between Dr. Karadzic and Nenad Stevandic that's 65 ter 1D02696, again a conversation that took place well in advance of 1995 when the steps were implemented --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you give the number again. There's six digits on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you give the number again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, sorry. 1D02696.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a conversation between Nenad Stevandic and Radovan Karadzic that took place in August of 1991, and on page 1 in Serbian and page 1 -- page 1 in English and in page 1 going onto page 2 in Serbian. Let's go to page 2, I think, of the Serbian. Stevandic says: "Well, Andjelko and Vojo are going for it full tilt quite recklessly. Brdjanin would like to put a stop to it, have a bit of consultation and reasoning." Dr. Karadzic tells Stevandic: "Tell them not to do anything stupid on any account because then we are accused of these stupidities." Goes on to explain that Alija doesn't have any arguments against the Serbs. He says that he doesn't want to reach an understanding with the Serbs, so don't provide him with any arguments.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We move on to page 2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And then Karadzic assures Stevandic: "We'll do everything Vojo and Brdjo think but after the failure of the agreements that Alija will bring about, we'll accuse Alija for this failure." So, Mr. Dodik, contrary to the suggestion that what Dr. Karadzic said in 1995 - simply a PR exercise - this is a contemporaneous reflection of his assurance to his followers that he had the plans and they would be implemented at the opportune moment; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what Karadzic is saying really made sense at the time. It was quite rational. As you see, he is saying that nothing stupid should be done and that no one should take any particular measures and this should be positive, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we're clear on the relationship between Karadzic and Stevandic, you were asked about -- or you've mentioned Mr. Stevandic in your tape-recorded interview in July of 2003, and that's 65 ter 33531. And here was the exchange that followed and what you said about Stevandic. The question was: "Now, this Nenad Stevandic, a 23-year-old medical student and the president of the Sokol Society --" And you said: "Yes, I know the name. He was very -- I know him. He was very present at the manifestations of all sorts that we're asking to get support for this fight that they were talking about all the time and he acted in co-ordination with all these people who --"

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: But excuse me, I don't have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... quite right. Please, let's turn to page 11 of the English and 13 of the Serbian and on both pages it appears at the bottom third of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask something still?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may ask something if it is an appropriate question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, everything is appropriate. I'm not sure when and with whom this was recorded. Who was I having this interview with? In 1993, you recorded me ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik, this is the same interview we looked at and went through yesterday at some length, the one that Mr. Grady -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh yes, but how can it be from 1993 then?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, 2003 was the date --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second. You said -- oh 2003. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. Can we move one more page on the Serbian, please. Sorry, Madam Registrar, it's the page that has the ERN at the top L0102603, so should be ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That seems to be the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And one more page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your answer begins down ... at the bottom of that page and continues on the top. Oh ... no, it's still not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: One more attempt at that. Can I see the ERN on this, please, 2602 -- turn back to 2602, please. There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And it begins with the first question that's by the name "PG." "Now this Nenad Stevandic, a 23-year-old medical student and the president of the Sokol Society --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move in English to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: "Yes, I know the name. He was very -- I know him. He was very present at the manifestations of all sorts that were asking to get support for this fight that they were talking about all the time, and he acted in co-ordination with all these people who were in the police and ... the authorities." And then Mr. Grady asked: "Did you know his relationship between Radovan Karadzic, himself and Radovan Karadzic." "I know that there -- their relationship was very close, and, since people in Banja Luka knew that he was closely linked with Karadzic, I think that gave Stevandic a great deal of power in Banja Luka." And do you stand by those answers in July of 2003, Mr. Dodik?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how that looked.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And I would also tender 1D02696, the document we looked at a moment earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 1D02696 receives number P7763.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dodik, yesterday you were asked toward the end of your examination-in-chief about the assembly session at which the six strategic goals were discussed, and you spoke briefly about the goals as political goals. Then you were then asked about any kind of plan, oral or written, for Muslims to be -- Muslims and Croats to be expelled from territories under Serbian control, and you said that it was not a goal, not even an unwritten one. I want to ask you a few questions about those issues. Now, first of all, you must have been aware that the strategic objectives were being implemented by the Army of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army had its role that was provided by the law in the constitution. It's defined there what the role of the army was. Of course, in every country, in every state, the army implements the decisions of the highest organs and bodies, first of all, the legislative ones and the parliament. So in the broadest terms, yes. The army in Republika Srpska primarily had to defend the people in the territory of Republika Srpska from the Muslim aggression and later the joint Muslim/Croat aggression, and that was the primary goal of the army. That was how I understood it and how I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 11809, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And this is an interview in the beginning of February 1993 in Novi Glas of General Milovanovic. For your benefit, Mr. Dodik, if you can direct your attention to the third paragraph down on the next page in English, in the left column, sorry -- and it's the -- the third column ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we -- can you scroll farther to the left, please. Thank you. Now this third column. Down -- the -- the first column left third row down. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: There, General Milovanovic states: "So far, our army has achieved four strategic goals, that is, the tasks. It has fulfilled four tasks, thus enabling the political leadership in the country to work. We have created the basis so that everybody knows that we exist, regardless of whether somebody recognises us or not, and that is the basis from which we embark on the negotiations." And that, Mr. Dodik, is a reflection of the army's active implementation of the strategic goals which were seen as advancing the Bosnian Serb bargaining position and negotiations; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the armies still do in the world to this day, so it's no wonder. The armies intervene in Syria even today and then the negotiations follow. So certainly it's the legitimate task of the army, and I think that Mr. Milovanovic has really put it well, and I support him in what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender 65 ter 11809.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 11809 receives number P7764.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dodik, with respect to what was encompassed by the strategic objectives or how they were to be implemented, you did not participate in the direct formulation of the strategic objectives with President Karadzic and General Mladic when they met on that subject, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not with them personally, but I was at assembly sessions which decided it; and I don't even know when the two of them met, if they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you weren't present at meetings when Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik met with General Mladic and the corps commanders to discuss the implementation of the strategic objectives; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you didn't receive the directives that followed those meetings; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended assembly sessions and I know approximately what was discussed. Of course, there are all documents about it. I did not receive directives from anyone. At the time, I was an independent MP in the assembly as I told you before. I had only contact with the group of deputies in the assembly. I did not participate in any other forms of decision-making.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to the some of the assembly sessions in that case. During the course of those assembly sessions, Mr. Dodik, did you hear any indications of an intention or a goal or the process of expelling Muslims and Croats? Any hints about that at all during those sessions, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was talk and discussions about the war operations and the conflict that was going on, but I never heard that as a discussion about ethnic cleansing. All the time, from the moment the war began, there were constant demands in the assembly to clearly define goals and to have in mind very clearly what the purpose of that war was. Most of these demands came from deputies -- from constituencies that the Serbs had to flee, such as the valley of the Neretva river, where people who had to leave their homes --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the question is not: Tell me about all the things you did hear notice assembly sessions in connection with the war. The question was whether you heard any hints or suggestions at all during those sessions about an intention or goal or the process of moving or expelling Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you mentioned earlier that you were present at the assembly session at which the strategic goals were announced. I take it that's a reference to the 16th Assembly Session on May 12th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no -- yes, the 12th of May. That session was held in Banja Luka; right? I think I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was no need to interrupt Mr. Tieger. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, this Chamber has received in evidence the transcript from the 16th Session at which the strategic objectives were enunciated and explained by Dr. Karadzic, and the VRS was established, General Mladic named as chief of the Main Staff, and so on. After Dr. Karadzic enunciated and explained the objectives, do you recall hearing any mention of or discussion about the "conquests" that were necessary in any places where Serbs were not a majority?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any such thing absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. And specifically do you remember reference by the delegate from Brcko about the need for conquests, in particular in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Brcko was an important communication hub. I think it was a legitimate goal, but not from the point of view of ethnic cleansing but from the point of view of compactness and communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it's a bit unclear whether this is a -- whether you heard about -- whether you remember a reference by the delegate from Brcko about the need for conquests. Could you please answer that question directly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge, it was a long time ago. I did not review all those transcripts. I suppose there was such talk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the only question was whether you remember; apparently you do not. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Do you remember hearing any representative express satisfaction that the strategic objectives confirmed that Muslims already removed from a Muslim-majority municipality would not be coming back?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but again I don't remember. A long time has passed. It's possible though that there was such talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This Chamber has already received -- has also received in evidence the transcript of the very next session held in late July 1992 - that's P4581 - and, in particular, has received evidence of Mr. Dukic's remarks --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For the benefit of the parties, that's at page 71 in English and page 72 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- referring to Birac and noting: "If we move further, there is Birac which is 100 to 108 kilometres away and has 120.000 Muslims. That is how many there were, but I hope that has at least been halved. And --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's best to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I think we -- Mr. Dukic, at least visible, is starting speaking at the bottom of this page in English. Is it the next page where we can find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, next page in English, certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And are we on the right page in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Start on the right page and we also have to move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the middle of the page from where you read, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Next page in Serbian page, the one marked 75. One more page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking aloud. Yes, now we are on the right page in English at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is a short quote, Mr. Dukic -- excuse me, Mr. Dodik. Mr. Dukic expressing the point that Birac had 120.000 Muslims, at least that's how many there were, but expressing the hope that that had at least been halved. Did you hear that expression from Mr. Dukic who was the president of the SDS Executive Board and the co-ordinator of the Birac SAO?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've said that I wasn't a member of the SDS, and I couldn't have heard that. I did not hear it from Mr. Dukic. I don't remember. I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to another assembly session. Perhaps you recall this comment then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik, I'm a bit puzzled by your observation you couldn't have heard it because you were not a SDS member. This is an assembly session which is not exclusively for SDS members. So therefore, I'm puzzled by your explanation as why you couldn't have heard it, apart from whether you did hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Coming up on --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because Mr. Tieger said that Rajko Dukic was the president of the Executive Board of the SDS, so on those grounds I couldn't, whereas at the assembly sessions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Tieger was quoting from an assembly session, a quote from a person who had functions within the SDS as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. What we have on the screen now is a tape-recording of the 22nd Session of the RS Assembly held on the 23rd and 24th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 78 in the English and page 76 in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We see the remarks of Mr. Malojevic directed to the proposed Law on Citizenship, and if we look at the second paragraph in English and the third paragraph down in -- in the -- in the second -- the first paragraph in Serbian, Mr. Malojevic makes this point: "Second, the citizenship of Republika Srpska shall be acquired among other things by birth in the territory of Republika Srpska. This refers to all the Muslims and Croats we expelled, in reality they are citizens of Republika Srpska ..." Now, Mr. Dodik, that's an indication, isn't it, that -- of an intention or goal or process of removing Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't even remember who that gentleman was. How could I know what he said? I don't know what was adopted in the form of law later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, do you recall, as we see later on in that page, that on the basis of Mr. Malojevic's remarks that proposed Law on Citizenship was sent back for review?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says. Why would I have to remember all that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik, you don't have to remember anything. If you remember, you should tell us what you remember; if you don't remember, tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I would tender that excerpt, it is part of P7196 -- oh, sorry. My mistake. This is already part of that existing excerpted portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So nothing --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- needed to be done. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me turn, then, to 65 ter 02382, another assembly session, Mr. Dodik, this one the 34th. And if we could turn to page 33 in the English and 31 in the B/C/S, in the Serbian, we find the remarks of Mr. Milinkovic. And he appears to be expressing satisfaction about what has been achieved and reminding others of that. And he says, in about the third sentence of his remarks: "Gentlemen, I would like to hear which municipality, let alone region, is loosing a bigger part of the territory than gaining compared to the percentage of Muslims and Croats who live [sic] there." "I understand from Herzegovina that it is painful to lose the Neretva valley and part are the Nevesinje and Trebinje municipalities, but I never heard anyone saying they were pleased that 30 per cent of Muslims in Trebinje municipality was wiped out, same in Gacko, 20 per cent in Nevesinje, 20 per cent in Bileca, that the hydroelectric plant on Trebisnjica and electric power plant in Gacko are left to Serbs." And he goes on to ask: "Should we be this dissatisfied?" And then turning to page 34 of the English and 32 of the Serbian he continues: "Gentlemen, there is no Serbian state in Bosnian pot without gradual depopulation and relocating. If we want ethnically pure Serbian state, and we do, don't we" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not see the text in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That should be in the middle of the page on 32, approximately -- well, it's hard to measure the lines, but beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: B/C/S we have page 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It should be 32. I thought I indicated we should move to 32 -- oh, it's e-court page 32. I'm sorry, but I realise they almost correspond to the hard copy pagination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought we had it on the last page, but I'm not quite sure but I saw the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now it's the wrong page -- this is hard -- this is e-court page 32, hard copy page 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One page back therefore. I do see approximately in the middle at the last word of a line a reference to "gentlemen."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately just above the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. And thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Again the quote is: "Gentlemen, there is no Serbian state in Bosnian pot without gradual depopulation and relocating. If we want ethnically pure Serbian state - and we do, don't we? - if we all know and emphasise that we cannot live with them, then we have to realise that these draft maps are offering exactly that and there has to be relocation." Now do you assert that you didn't hear this reference to the desirability of Muslim departures and what had happened to that point?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it would be fair, Your Honours, for the Prosecutor, when putting to me these transcripts to first confirm my presence at these sessions so that we can discuss it. I don't even know who this man was. I don't think he was even a deputy, a delegate. It's possible that some people who were not deputies still spoke at some assembly sessions, but I don't remember this man. And especially if it's written in the transcript that I was not present at that session, I don't think it would be fair for you to question me about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you have any recollection about your presence, please tell us. You think -- you've heard the date, isn't it; and otherwise Mr. Tieger will repeat it. If you say, I don't remember that I was present, please tell us, no problem. Mr. Tieger, the date of the assembly session was?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please put on your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: 27th through 29th of August, 1993, and the 30th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just to be clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Locations?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Oh. Look at the cover. Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you've got the dates, you have got the place. Do you have any recollection as whether you were present or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked the Prosecutor to read from the transcript whether I was at that session --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Witness, I asked you a question. Would you please answer that question. Do you remember that you were present at that meeting on those days, assembly meetings, held in Jahorina. Would you please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked you that. There were several sessions at Jahorina, several sessions. I can't confirm whether I was at this particular one, but it's written in the transcript. Why are you trying to run away from it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're not running away from anything, but we're insisting on you answering questions that are put to you. So you don't remember specifically whether you were present at these meetings. Mr. Tieger, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just before we break, I want to look at one more session, the 37th Session of the Assembly of Republika Srpska; that's 65 ter 02388.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you, just at the outset, tell the date and the location to avoid any further questions about that. Obviously 10th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As His Honour Judge Fluegge just indicated, that session was held on the 10th of January, 1994, and in -- in Pale, Mr. Dodik. And if we turn to page 110 of the English and page 82 in the Serbian, we see Dr. Karadzic speaking and he says the following -- and this is ... yeah, you should see that toward the upper portion of your page and this appears just about the middle of the page in English. "I know that at the time when we had some unfinished tasks related to military actions, I just prayed to God that nothing be accepted because we had some tasks to complete." And then he says it is a good time for us to make peace now. And then explains: "I was worried a bit that we would not be able to get more than 50 per cent of the territory that we chose. For example, in Doboj the Muslims were in the relative majority. At the census before the last one, we were in the relative majority, but this census speaks about a relative Muslim majority. Nowadays Doboj is almost 100 per cent Serbian. The people from mountains moved in the town, and so on. We are not out of danger, we are in great danger, and it is for our benefit that all this ended. The end does not suit the Muslims." So, Mr. Dodik, when you indicated earlier that you hadn't heard anything at assembly sessions that provided an indication of an intention or goal or process of removing Muslims and Croats, did you have in mind the remarks of Dr. Karadzic that there had been unfinished tasks related to military actions and specifically ones that resulted in the demographic change in Doboj from being a majority to being almost 100 per cent Serbian?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before the witness answers that question -- Witness, do you have any recollection as having been present at the assembly session of the 10th of January, 1994, in Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir, I did not expect this. At Pale there were at least four or five sessions. I can't remember the dates, and I asked you kindly when putting this document to me to see in the transcript whether my name is there or not. This way, you are maltreating me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not maltreating you. In these transcripts, there's no systematic --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Neither is the Prosecutor. You said there were at least five. Do you remember, were you present at all five in Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I remember that I attended some of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Dodik, I am testing your claim about what could be gleaned about the existence of any intention or plan or process of removing Muslims from what was said at the assembly sessions, so I am asking you what sorts of remarks at assembly sessions you had in mind when you said that. And now I'm asking you if you remembered this particular remark by Dr. Karadzic when you asserted that there were no indications of such an intention or goal or process at the assembly sessions.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would tender that excerpt, and I see it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before you give that a number, I also -- to keep it chronological, I should also tender the previous excerpts from the 34th Session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It should be added to P2508.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The previous one or this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The ones from the 34th, which was 65 ter 02382, that should be added to P2508 and this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Too quick. Madam Registrar, is that clear to you what should be added?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sure the Prosecution will notify me of the pages when they're uploaded and put in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And now I would tender these excerpts from 65 ter 02388.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Still to be excerpted?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, would you reserve a number for the excerpts still to be uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that will be added to -- it should be added to P3076.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it still has to be uploaded and then should be added to --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would appreciate notification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I may indicate that I will be concluding very quickly after we return, so for the benefit of my colleagues and the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Very quickly, Mr. Tieger, meaning 15 minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't think it will be more than 15 minutes, but in that area of -- I mean, in -- I won't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I won't be using my -- the full amount of my allotted time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Dodik, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes because we'll take a break and we will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Dodik. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik, it doesn't really change the question of what you had in mind when you said there were no indications at the assembly sessions, but I did attempt to track down assembly session records in response to your point, and I wanted to show you 65 ter 2870 which is an attendance lists of deputies from the 16th Session through the 35th Session, I believe. And if we look at item 21 we see your name, and it indicates you as -- and this indicates the number of the sessions from which the deputy was absent - and a funny way of putting it - indicates that you were absent from the 17th Session -- actually, seems to list that twice; from the 20th -- the 22nd Session; and from the second part of the 34th, which has about three different periods but the question I asked you about was from the first part of that session. So if that clarifies for you whether or not the records indicate your presence or absence at some of the sessions we discussed, there it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I'm happy to tender that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Oh, before we do, could we turn to page 2 in the English, before we leave this document. I just wanted to look at one item.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And at number 55, we see, again, Djokoslav Milinkovic who I believe you said was not a deputy but who, in fact, appears to be a deputy?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In all fairness to the witness I think that he said that he thought he was not even a deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But didn't give certain information. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. So I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry, just one observation. Mr. Dodik did not mention Milinkovic but Milojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be another -- I do remember it was I think on the same -- we'll check that, I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And with regard to the 30s -- oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you first -- you were tendering it. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 20870 receives number P7765.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7765 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- with regard to the 37th Session, which we discussed and I think was also the subject of your inquiry about whether or not you were present and whether or not you spoke, in fact, Mr. Dodik, the records indicate -- a record of the session indicates that you did speak at the early part of the session. However, if we turn to 65 ter 2388, in English page 65 and Serbian page 49, the chairman, Mr. Krajisnik, indicates: "At that stage in the proceedings we have to do a roll-call in order to see how many deputies are present." He starts indicating how many are gone. Nedjo Gavric is done, Milorad Kuzmanovic was feeling bad, et cetera, and then after the notation about polemics from the seat he says: "I have to note this down into the minutes because we agreed that without a consultation - is Dodik here? - if you allow me I would say something that I'm entitled to. It is very irresponsible behaviour of the deputies to leave the session self-willingly because it very often happens that we do not have a quorum present. It is my suggestion that we conclude that Gavric left without permission and Dodik has well." So it appears that you were gone by that point in the session, Mr. Dodik, and the portion of Mr. Karadzic's remarks that I directed your attention to earlier occurred after that point in the session. So if that answers your questions about attendance. I have a couple of additional assembly sessions I wanted to draw your attention to. This Chamber has received in evidence some of Dr. Karadzic's remarks at the 53rd Assembly Session and that's 65 ter -- that's P4584, where Mr. Karadzic said: "We've drawn some maps into which a part of the Neretva valley could be integrated and, of course, access to the sea, the Drina, should be clean. These are all priorities. The corridor must be wide." And then if we could turn to 65 ter 02380 at page 49 in the English and page 40 in the Serbian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And these are the beginning of Mr. Krajisnik's remarks in the middle of the page in English and toward the bottom quarter of the page in Serbian. And Mr. Krajisnik says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think -- please check if that is the right page in English. At the middle of the page Mr. Kupresanin is speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, it's Mr. Krajisnik, chairman, and he says: "Vojo Kupresanin has asked me" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I missed that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik says: "Vojo Kupresanin has asked me a question. I believe that there is one thing that we must understand. We have strategic aims and how angry do you think the Herzegovinians will be because the Neretva is not our border and how angry they will be because the Drina is not clear and how angry they will be because a part of Sarajevo is no more?" Now, Mr. Dodik, those are both expressions at the assembly sessions about the need to have a clean Drina area which included Muslim-majority areas, Muslim-majority municipalities, within that area; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there were Muslims in Podrinje, just like there were Serbs in Sarajevo. The war produced the same result on both sides practically, and it was that people had to leave their original places of residence and move to some other locations. If a calculation were made, you could see that the number of people on either side was practically identical, so we cannot say that it was the Serbs who expelled the Serbs from Sarajevo; but I think that from the beginning we could have worked in a decent manner. You can see the evidence of my presence here. I feel that you wanted to manipulate me by presenting me quotations, noting my absence. I'm addressing myself to the Prosecutor. I did not attend some sessions but you asked me about them. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Witness, when answering a question, you're giving an answer to a question put to you by the Prosecutor and you're addressing the Chamber, and I invited you earlier to refrain from the kind of commentaries you did. I do that again. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I can answer some questions if I remember and if I was present, but to be expected to comment on something that was said when I was absent, this I can't do. As far as this is concerned, well, Krajisnik himself has said everything. I don't remember those speeches of his. The sessions were always tense, very emotional. Many people took the floor and the atmosphere was very different, if you compare what was being said at the beginning in 1991 and then later in 1995. As a rule, it depended on the developments on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Dodik, first of all, you had an opportunity to look at the assembly sessions and in the attendance record that we reviewed, which appeared to reflect your attendance at the 33rd Session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: But in any event, I tender that excerpt Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And it should be added to P7359 [Realtime transcript read in error "P7539"].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that is sufficient information for you that this excerpt uploaded under this 65 ter number should be added to P7539 -- then I read from the ... 7539. And you're instructed to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik, you just said that people had to leave their original places of residence and move to some other locations. That's because in the case of Muslims from Podrinje that the Bosnian Serb -- Serbs claimed that area, including Muslim-majority municipalities, as reflected in the comments by Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik, that the Drina must be clean; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're manipulating again. I said that the Serbs from Sarajevo had also left --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you may answer a question. I said again and again you should refrain from accusation of manipulation. And I also instructed you not to seek eye contact with the Defence, which you did several times now this morning. Would you please -- please be aware that by this behaviour that may have an effect on the evaluation of your evidence. You're here and we'd like to hear your evidence and to fully consider it. Would you please keep that in mind. I said so three minutes ago, I said so ten minutes ago, so now I expect you to refrain from doing the same. You may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember these speeches by Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, you -- the strategic objectives and specifically strategic objective number 3, and the need for the -- a clean Drina included Muslim-majority municipalities like, for example, Gorazde; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't how I understood it. It was not set down anywhere when I took part in deciding on that and in discussions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at another excerpt from the 33rd Assembly. Again, 65 ter 02380. Page 40 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I do so I may give some additional guidance to you. If Mr. Tieger puts something to you, instead of saying that's manipulation, if you disagree, fine, then you say, Mr. Tieger, I do not agree with that because this is how it was. That's -- without accusations giving the testimony we would expect you to without the aggressivity in your answers. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We're going to look at another excerpt from the 33rd Assembly Session, this one at page 40 of the English, page 33 of the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And it's from July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct. And -- but we've fortunately had a chance to look as well at the assembly session attendance records and -- which are now in evidence for that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And this is Mr. Karadzic speaking and you'll find --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry for interrupting you. I said it's from July 1993. It was wrongly recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And Dr. Karadzic says the following: "Gorazde is ours. Perhaps we will have to make some concessions in parts of Sarajevo itself for Gorazde to remain ours because the Drina is of enormous importance for Republika Srpska and for the Serbian people and lastly it is one of the strategic aims for the Drina not to be a border. That is what we adopted here in this Assembly." And that's a reflection of the fact, Mr. Dodik, that Muslim-majority municipalities like Gorazde were embraced by the strategic objectives and considered to be Bosnian Serb; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, here you have Karadzic's speech. I do not agree that it was primarily defined as such and that at the end of the war Gorazde remained on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender this excerpt, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's an excerpt which should be added to something or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, to P6921.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar informs me that it is already part of exhibit and perhaps, Madam Registrar, you give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the excerpt currently used by the Prosecutor is currently Exhibit P7359. That's page 33 and 34 of the B/C/S and page 40 and 41 of the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Tiger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now a little earlier we talked of P7539. Is this the same P number? Earlier it was given 7539 instead of 7359.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I think that was a transposition of the numbers. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which now is the accurate one? Madam Registrar, you --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit is P7359.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's hereby confirmed now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Dodik, this will be my last questions to you. I put it to you, sir, that it is on the basis of this type of information that we've just looked at - some of which you heard directly because you were present at sessions, some of which was known to the other assembly members who were present, and was readily accessible to you and on the basis of similar information which was available either through representatives of the international community or any number of people with whom you had contact - on the basis of such information that you once accused the Bosnian Serb leadership at all levels of organised war crimes and you did that publicly; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have information about that. Possibly in some political discussions, but I don't stand by that any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's look at 65 ter 33540.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we look at that you said: "I did not have information about that." What did you exactly mean by "that"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm seeking clarification of your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, yes. I did not receive information about this so then, of course, I cannot stand by this claim. But I can't deny that I may perhaps have said something like that, but it could have been in some political showdown or in some other similar situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let's that I can one step at a time. Again I asked for 33540. This is from the BBC. It's the text of a report by Serbian news agency Beta dated the 12th of January, 2001. "Outgoing Serb Republic Prime Minister Milorad Dodik today accused the Serb Democratic Party (SDS) of 'organising and committing crimes during the war' in Bosnia-Herzegovina. "'It must be openly said that crimes have been committed in this region under the SDS leadership and this must be punished,' Dodik said. He said that it was to be expected that 'all leading SDS officials at various levels stand before The Hague Tribunal'." Now you were asked about that during the course of your -- about this article during the course of your testimony in the Karadzic case, and you said at transcript page 36903 through -04: "Yes, that was the political struggle between me and the SDS in 2001. It was a time of transition of power. You can consider this as political discourse which need not necessarily be based on facts but I'm not denying having said this." And then again at transcript page 36906 you said: "I didn't deny what the BBC says." Does that remain your position, Mr. Dodik, that you don't deny having said these things but you chalk them up to politics?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely what I said in the quotation that you read out from the Karadzic trial, I do stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, does that mean that what you were saying was true but you decided to say it for political reasons, political advantage; or that what you were saying was not true but you decided for political reasons to accuse the SDS of organised war crimes?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means what you quoted from the Karadzic trial, so you may quote it again if you like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please answer the question. Mr. Tieger put to you two possible interpretations of what you said and asked which of the two it is. Could you please answer that question? Is it not true but you said it just for political reasons; or is it true but you expressed yourself on the matter for political gain or political reasons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were people who committed crimes and they ought to be prosecuted and some have been prosecuted, and I do stand by that and it is part of the truth. But the other part, an abstract qualification of all leading persons from the SDS, could be treated as a political statement. There were persons who participated; some courts have proved their participation and they ought to be published. That's what I said and what I said here as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you were clear that this open accusation that needed to be said, must be openly said, included the top-level SDS leadership, right, because you explicitly excluded Mrs. Plavsic from that characterisation; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how this reads, yes. I do think that she was not a very important person in those processes within the SDS, and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have nothing further, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could I really get a real answer to the last question. You excluded Madam Plavsic. Does that mean that, apart from her, that your accusation covered also the level at which Madam Plavsic was functioning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not accuse anyone. I was expressing my political view on this. In the case of Biljana Plavsic when I said that she did not have an important role in the SDS leadership, as I said here in this text --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... let me -- you're moving away from my question. Whether you call it your view on the matter or whether you accused -- excluding or making an exception for Madam Plavsic suggests that in your view or your accusation - whatever you would like to call it - that you covered the top level of the SDS. Is that how we can understand it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, Your Honour, I said a moment ago that there were people, both at the local level of the SDS and others, who were involved in crimes and should be convicted, and I still think so today. As far as Biljana Plavsic is concerned, it's exactly as I said here: She did not play an important part in the leadership of the party.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, you are not -- I try it for a last time to see whether I now get an answer to my question. You said: "I said a moment ago that there were people, both at the local level of the SDS and others ..." Did "others" include the top level of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot say that. That's for the Court to determine, but I believe that there was involvement even of the people who were part of the top leadership.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I would tender 65 ter 33540, Mr. President, and that concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 33540 receives number P7766.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Mr. Lukic, are you ready to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's keep this document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dodik, we have this BBC report before us. You have just been asked about the criminal liability of SDS members. Did you ever deal with investigations and determining the culpability of people from the top leadership of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am neither trained nor authorised to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to make one correction at page -- yesterday's transcript, page 42260, 23rd line, it was noted that Mr. Dodik said he give 6.000 various political statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which number did you mention?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have 02366, 65 ter number, on our screens, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- oh, it's added to that. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the record of the 24th Session of the National Assembly of Republika Srpska from 8 January 1993. Page 9 was shown to you. Page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in English and page 64 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it was put to you that proposals were made for Muslims not to be recognised as a nation. I would need the beginning of this contribution of Vojo Kupresanin to see why this was contested. Mr. Kupresanin says, I quote: "We stumbled over some concepts more than once in the past. Gentlemen, is the Muslim nation a nation at all? The nation that was manufactured and introduced by a concept of Tito's in 1974, receives a position like the Greeks, to say the least. Should we throw out this nation as a nation, and say instead that they are Serb people of Muslim faith?" Mr. Dodik, you are a young man, just as I. Before 1974, do you remember how Muslims in Bosnia-Herzegovina identified themselves, how did they declare themselves?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As Serbs and Croats, or Croats of their particular faith. Meso Selimovic, a famous author, declared himself as a Serb and many documents exist about that. Ivo Andric, the Nobel Prize winner, did the same and many other intellectuals as well --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the following sentence. Could ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have to stop here. We don't receive interpretation because the interpreters missed a sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, the English interpretation stopped at one point and I can continued to listen to you in B/C/S. It was stopped when you said: "Ivo Andric ... did the same as did many other intellectuals ..."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Until 1974 in documents in the former Yugoslavia, Muslims were marked as a religious group with a small letter m. From 1974, the letter m became a capital and it was decided that they should be designated as a nation, and that what's Vojo Kupresanin is saying. And it was only in 1993 by a decision of the Bosniak Assembly, I believe it was called in Sarajevo, that people receives the name Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which indicates that they themselves had a problem with their self-identification in 1991/1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you telling Mr. Dodik that's what happened or are you asking him a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that is he telling us this. I asked a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It was you who is speaking? Am I right? Oh. I'm sorry. The record is different. Thank you. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we briefly see P7662. That's the record of the 38th Session. I have P7662.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think you are referring to P7762.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour. Yes, you are right. 7762. Yes. I apologise. We need page 74 in English version and page 57 in B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was put to you that Mr. Karadzic talked about the implementation of pre-planned steps. In this connection, I'll just mention the number P6999 was also shown you to, page 3 in English and page 2 in B/C/S. Before the war, did Serbs in their political struggle violate the constitutional rights of Muslims and Croats in those pre-planned moves of theirs?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no such evidence. I don't think that happened. I believe, moreover, that several attempts were made in many ways to reach an agreement. Well-known is the situation with the so-called Cutileiro Plan, where the leadership of the Serbs accepted the proposed organisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a complex community. Alija Izetbegovic agreed too, as did the Croatian side. That meeting was in Portugal. But when Alija Izetbegovic returned to Sarajevo he rejected the plan, while the Serbian side never rejected it; but it was impossible to put it in place because Alija Izetbegovic rejected it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I'm a bit puzzled by -- in your question you include the pre-planned moves, whereas - if I understood the witness well - he denied that there were any pre-planned moves. So, therefore, to -- but perhaps I may have misunderstood it, but if you would clarify that because what Mr. Tieger put to him wasn't this an example of pre-planned moves on what happened. The witness always said no -- at least that's how I understood him. Could you please clarify this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will try to find in the transcript and come back to that topic, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To conclude this discussion, did you see any action by the Serbian side as action to which Muslims and Croats responded; or was it the case that Muslims and Croats made moves to which Serbs responded in that their action?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political and military moves in that time were made exclusively by Muslims and Croats. As for the events that I was involved in, I see them as a reaction to that -- to those moves and to the political decisions they made after Republika Srpska was established, together with all the rest that was necessary to defend the people, first of all, the people that was exposed almost in equal measure on all sides in Krajina, around Sarajevo, and in Herzegovina. Of course, I mean to say that there was awareness of the fact that the Muslims were suffering too, but it's a fact that it was a war, and we did not even have enough information about the suffering of people on the other side. So all those political and military actions were primarily a reaction to the situation that was already in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which side aimed to preserve the status quo, that is to say, the existing situation. Which side instead wanted to change the state? Which side, in other words, was forced to take action?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The first part of the question was fair and then Mr. Lukic went on to draw the conclusion for the witness that he wanted the witness to confirm. That's a very leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think my question was open, which side --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it was not -- yes. If you say which side did this, and this, and this, then you assume that happened. And that makes it a leading question, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I'll rephrase things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Mr. Lukic. Of course -- and could you also make clear in your questions. I think the status quo, the status quo of what exactly? Because the witness has testified several times that the Serbian side very much wished to remain within the Yugoslav -- Yugoslavia, whereas the Muslims wanted to move out. At the same time - but that's a totally different matter - the status quo, that is, who controls what territory on the ground in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Could we please try to clearly distinguish between the two, because in your question, it's -- it's really seeking a lot of confusion. So could you please -- and even I wonder whether there's any disagreement about that among the parties. I think that, Mr. Tieger, whether the Serbs wanted to stay in -- in Yugoslavia and whether the Serbs wanted to have certain control over certain territories, I never felt - but perhaps I'm missing something - that there's disagreement about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, it depends to some extent on the time-period, but basically there's no essential disagreement. And in addition, I think it's largely a rehash of what was covered in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not a rehash of what's covered in the direct examination. It is answering to the whole line of questions who actually took actions and who took reactions, who had plans and who did not have plans.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and we do -- we are not assisted by putting that all together and asking for the status quo. It depends on status quo of what exactly, at what point in time. If you want to further clarify it and if you think that that's not clear yet, then you have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We've heard -- it's not in dispute that you've said that the Muslim/Croat side was in favour of Bosnia separating from Yugoslavia and the Serbs were against that. In this situation, according to you, who had to have the active role? And what did you see on the ground in that respect? Who had an active role? Were the Serbs actively trying to stay in Yugoslavia? Or was it that Muslims and Croats were actively trying to separate, to secede?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD DODIK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The active role was the role of Muslims and Croats, and that's what I explained earlier, talking about the unilateral secession of Slovenia and Croatia from Yugoslavia. That was obvious even in mid-1991 when in Bosnia-Herzegovina nothing indicated it was in the offing. Such support also -- such support by foreign countries to Slovenia and Croatia was also a requirement for Bosnia and Herzegovina to do so the same. And if you look at the dates, you will see that the decisions of the Serb people were always a reaction to what was going on around them. It can be evidently seen from the chronology and the chronology proves it. As for plans or lack of plans, when you are put in a position where you have to make a decision, then you have to think about what to do. In that context, almost all of us, regardless of whether we were told to do so or not, we had to do something. We had to constitute a republic. If you constitute a republic, then you have to adopt a constitution and laws. That's the logic of events. Of course, you can interpret it as a sort of pre-conceived action, but it was simply a necessity. The decision of Muslims and Croats led to a unilateral secession contrary to local legislation. It was just a reflection of the political will of the political representatives of Muslims and Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina. There were no state decisions made to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Dodik. It's time for the break. I'll try to finish as soon as I can in the next session so that you can return to your normal obligations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break. Could you follow the usher, Mr. Dodik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And before we take that break, Mr. Lukic, you tried to finish as soon -- Mr. Mladic, would you refrain from communicating with the public gallery. Mr. Lukic, as soon as possible means what?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope I will finish in less than half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Less than half an hour. That would also mean that -- I do understand that the next witness was scheduled to arrive not later than 1.00, but we might need him a little bit earlier. And is there any news about his availability before 1.00, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Victims and Witness Section are doing their best to bring the witness earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll see whether he arrives in time so that we would not lose any further time. We take a break and resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps briefly, I think there was an issue about Mr. Malojevic and another person. At the same time I noted that Mr. Malojevic addressed the others as colleague deputies or so, so -- which is a suggestion that he was a deputy himself as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I leave that open and I don't think it's that vital that we should pursue the matter at this moment. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I owe you one reference too. When we discussed whether Mr. Dodik mentioned any actions, plans, on the Serbian side - and it was in connection with the document now P7762 - at page 3 of today's transcript, line 15, it was the question, and at line 20, Mr. Dodik said, I quote: "A. It was such a time that certainly we did make certain moves, and they were completely legitimate from the view of establishing Republika Srpska. Since Yugoslavia broke up using the people's right to self-determination, which was set out in the constitution of SFRY, the Serbs were entitled to have their own territorial organisation. That was how it was understood and how I understood it. So moves of this character constituting an entity were fully legitimate, but they were always a reaction to something else. That's also true."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it looks as if we are now ending up in argument. I think the emphasis was on the pre-planned. I leave it for the time being. I asked it because your question was not about moves but about pre-planned moves. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 02362 on our screens, please, and we need pages 78 in English version and 76 in B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document or these minutes talk about the citizenship of Republika Srpska, and you were presented this part where it is gained, inter alia, by birth. It's obvious that there was some uncertainty about this, so Slovenian and Croatian practice is invoked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need paragraph 4 in the B/C/S version and paragraph 5 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where it is said: "Just an example of how the Slovenes and the Croats did that." "We have various excerpts. In Slovenia, the Serbs signed loyalty papers but couldn't get citizenship. There is not a single Serb who was immediately granted citizenship in Slovenia even if he was born there. All they did was sign loyalty to the Republic of Slovenia." Do you remember now whether any of the Muslims or Croats were stripped of their citizenship because during the war they left the territory that was under the control of the Serbian forces during the war?
